statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. CME equity-index futures remain halted since the 21:00 UTC Friday settle, so no Nasdaq-100 price path exists in the current hour and Tail is held at the closed-venue floor of 5%. Stress eases one point to 54% because roughly ten hours have now passed since the last verified step in the US-Iran tanker exchange with no confirmed follow-on, and the IRGC counter-claim remains unconfirmed by CENTCOM. The scheduled 22:00 UTC Sunday reopen and the first full hour after it are the two WATCH slots of this horizon.
recommendation: Tail holds a 4-5% closed-venue floor through the dormant weekend hours and rises gradually to 13% into the final hour of the halt, so the deterministic mapping stays EA_ON and green for the first 22 published hours. The last two slots, the scheduled 22:00 UTC reopening hour and the first full hour after it, are each scored at 20% Tail and therefore map to WATCH and yellow; together they form the only published danger window. Stress runs from 54% down to a 52% low and then rebuilds to 70% at the reopen, entering the high band in the last four slots. Confidence declines from 85% to 74% as later slots rest on progressively older evidence.
headline: Nasdaq-100 unquoted at 29,544.15 through a second full day of the CME weekend halt as the Hormuz tanker exchange stays two-sided and unconfirmed; the scheduled 22:00 UTC reopen and the hour after it are the horizon's two WATCH slots
body:
The Nasdaq-100 closed the August payroll session on Friday 4 September at 29,544.15, up 61.85 points or 0.21% from a 29,482.30 previous close, having ranged between 29,440.15 and 29,655.22. QQQ closed the same session up 0.18%, and price retraced repeatedly in both directions inside that range, which is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement structure the Tail score measures. CME equity-index futures have been halted since the Friday settle and are scheduled to reopen at 22:00 UTC on 6 September. That reopening hour and the first full hour after it are the final two slots of this forecast.

The macro impulse into the halt is hawkish. August non-farm payrolls printed 162,000 against roughly 56,000 expected, with July revised up to a 21,000 gain and the unemployment rate steady at 4.1%. The 2-year yield rose about 5 basis points to 4.38%, its highest since January 2025, the 10-year added a basis point to 4.776% and the 30-year eased to 5.239%; the Federal Reserve H.15 release for 3 September carries 4.34%, 4.77% and 5.25% for the same maturities, which is consistent with that move. Rate futures shifted to price roughly a 59% probability of a hike at the 15-16 September FOMC, up from about 55% before the release. Equities absorbed the repricing calmly: the Nasdaq-100 held a small gain and VIX closed at 14.53 against a 14.32 previous close, inside a 13.80-14.58 range. A separate and still unresolved policy strand is the trade-embargo threat made late in Friday's session, which tied the prospect of embargoes on deficit partners to a demand for lower policy rates.

The geopolitical sequence has not advanced in roughly ten hours. US Central Command says American forces struck three Iranian crude oil tankers on Saturday morning after an aircraft carrier and a guided-missile destroyer were targeted by ballistic missiles; two vessels were permanently disabled and a third, unladen, was destroyed in the Gulf of Oman. Adm. Brad Cooper framed the action as a tanker-for-tanker economic cost and said the US would destroy Iran's oil fleet if necessary. The IRGC subsequently claimed it had targeted three oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and three US-affiliated vessels elsewhere, and separately claimed to have struck the US carrier and destroyer; CENTCOM says neither ship was hit and no servicemembers were injured, and the IRGC counter-claim remains unconfirmed. No verified follow-on step has been reported since. The campaign is therefore two-sided and unresolved rather than confirmed as an escalation ladder, which is why Stress carries it and Tail does not.

Cross-asset context remains conflicted rather than aligned. WTI is quoted near $91.5 after a weekly gain of roughly 9% and a monthly gain above 21%, an oil-led risk premium that pulls against equities. Friday's internals were rotational: every tracked semiconductor name rose, led by Micron and AMD, while five of eight megacaps fell, including Tesla, Apple and Microsoft, and delayed index futures closed split with NQ up 0.14% against ES down 0.42% and YM down 0.57%. Conflicting internals of that kind reduce directional conviction and belong in Stress, not in Tail.

The substantive change in this assessment is that the horizon now contains both the reopening auction and the hour that follows it. Roughly 49 hours of accumulated and so far unpriced information, an unresolved military exchange at a shipping chokepoint, an energy premium and untested hawkish rate pricing all meet a single opening auction rather than a continuous session. That concentration is scored as a 20% Tail allowance in each of the last two slots, which maps to WATCH and yellow and forms the only published danger window. It is a conditional gap-and-extension allowance, not an assertion that directional structure has been observed: an orderly two-way auction with genuine retracement would decay both scores quickly, while repeated extension after failed pullbacks would be the first genuine Tail amplifier of this sequence. Every earlier hour remains at the closed-venue floor and maps to EA_ON. The next seven-day calendar is led by PPI on Thursday 10 September and CPI on Friday 11 September, both at 12:30 UTC, with the 15-16 September FOMC beyond this window.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours cover the first full Saturday of the CME weekend halt, from 00:00 UTC to 23:00 UTC on 5 September. All 24 slots are available from published Claude assessments, every one is scored at the closed-venue Tail floor of 5% under a normal mode, and every one maps to EA_ON and green. Stress was flat at 38% from midnight through 10:00 UTC, climbed from 39% at 11:00 UTC to 42% by 14:00 UTC as the Saturday US-Iran sequence developed, stepped to 48% at 15:00 UTC once the CENTCOM tanker strikes were verified, rose to 52% by 19:00 UTC and peaked at 57% at 20:00 UTC when the Iranian counter-claim was published, then eased to 56% and 55% through the final slots as that claim went unconfirmed. Confidence held in a narrow 85-86% band throughout, reflecting a complete evidence set in which only the live price path was unavailable.
outlookSummary: Twenty-two of the twenty-four published hours fall inside the CME weekend halt, so no observable Nasdaq-100 price path can form in them; the mapped policy state stays EA_ON with Tail at a 4-5% closed-venue floor through the dormant hours, rising gradually from 06:00 UTC as Tel Aviv and Gulf Sunday cash sessions provide the first equity quotes since Friday and reaching 13% in the last full hour of the halt as a pre-auction gap allowance. The final two slots are different: futures are scheduled to reopen at 22:00 UTC on 6 September, so those hours are the first in which structure can exist. Each carries a 20% Tail allowance, maps to WATCH and yellow, and together they form the only published danger window. Stress opens at 54%, reaches a 52% low in the quietest overnight hours, rebuilds through the Sunday sessions and reaches 70% at the reopen, entering the high band in the last four slots. The drivers are a two-sided and unconfirmed Hormuz tanker campaign, an oil complex up roughly 9% on the week, hawkish September rate pricing after the 162K August payroll print, and an unresolved trade-embargo threat, none of which has met an equity quote since Friday. Confidence declines from 85% to 74% because later slots rest on progressively older evidence during an actively developing sequence. Orderly two-way retracement at the reopen would decay both scores quickly, while repeated extension after failed pullbacks would be the first genuine Tail amplifier.

forecast.analysis: Tail eases to the deep-halt floor of 4%. Asian cash venues do not trade on Sunday, so this is one of the quietest windows of the week for both price discovery and headline flow, and the conditional risk of a mean-reversion failure is close to its structural minimum.

forecast.analysis: The quiet continues. Stress remains in the elevated band rather than falling further because the underlying drivers are unresolved rather than absent: an active tanker campaign at a shipping chokepoint, an oil complex up about 9% on the week, and hawkish September rate pricing that has not met an equity quote since Friday.

forecast.analysis: Tel Aviv and Gulf cash markets trade on Sunday and begin to open around this hour, providing the first equity quotes anywhere since Friday's close. forecast.analysis: Stress ticks up as the Gulf and Israeli Sunday sessions establish opening levels. An orderly regional open would be mild evidence that the tanker exchange is being treated as contained; a sharp regional repricing would raise the dispersion the reopening auction has to absorb later in the day.
